# Purpose

`sales_analysis.R` is a single, self-contained analysis script. It generates a **synthetic** retail sales dataset (2,400 orders across 2025), cleans it, summarizes monthly revenue by product category, and saves a trend chart. It exists so the team can see a full, minimal example of a documented R workflow: data in, summary and chart out.

## Inputs

The script takes **no external input files**. All data is synthetic and generated inside the script:

```{r inputs, eval=FALSE}
set.seed(400)  # makes the synthetic data reproducible

n_orders <- 2400
sales <- tibble(
  order_id   = sprintf("ORD-%05d", 1:n_orders),
  order_date = as.Date("2025-01-01") + sample(0:364, n_orders, replace = TRUE),
  category   = sample(c("Grocery", "Household", "Snacks", "Beverages"),
                      n_orders, replace = TRUE,
                      prob = c(0.40, 0.25, 0.20, 0.15)),
  amount     = round(rlnorm(n_orders, meanlog = 3.9, sdlog = 0.45), 2)
)
```

**Dependencies:** `dplyr`, `ggplot2`, `lubridate` (install once with `install.packages()`).

## Processing Steps

1. **Clean** — defensively drop rows with non-positive amounts or missing dates:

```{r clean, eval=FALSE}
sales_clean <- sales %>%
  filter(amount > 0, !is.na(order_date))
```

2. **Summarize** — collapse orders to one row per month x category:

```{r summarise, eval=FALSE}
monthly_summary <- sales_clean %>%
  mutate(month = floor_date(order_date, "month")) %>%
  group_by(month, category) %>%
  summarise(revenue = sum(amount),
            orders  = n(),
            .groups = "drop")
```

3. **Visualize** — one line per category across the twelve months:

```{r plot, eval=FALSE}
trend_plot <- ggplot(monthly_summary,
                     aes(x = month, y = revenue, colour = category)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 1.6) +
  labs(title = "Monthly Revenue by Category (Synthetic Data, 2025)",
       x = "Month", y = "Revenue ($)", colour = "Category") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Outputs

| Output              | Type                  | Description                                        |
|---------------------|-----------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| `monthly_summary`   | data frame (48 rows)  | Revenue and order count per month per category     |
| `monthly_trend.png` | PNG image (9 x 5 in)  | Line chart of monthly revenue, one line per category |
| Console output      | text                  | First 8 rows of the summary, plus a completion message |

## How to Run

```{r run, eval=FALSE}
source("sales_analysis.R")
head(monthly_summary)
```

Because the data is seeded (`set.seed(400)`), every run reproduces identical numbers — a teammate can verify any figure by re-running the script.
